title: Tenant-windowed canary: environment-aware traffic shaping and auto-rollback profiles
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Implement a tenant-windowed canary orchestration feature that lets us schedule canary exposure windows per-tenant and per-environment (Hosted / Dedicated / Private). The feature should reconcile a canonical rollout intent into environment-specific traffic shaping profiles, enforce capacity and security constraints, and wire into the existing auto-rollback engine. This ticket covers design decisions, implementation tasks, tests, and rollout plan for the orchestration adapter and compatibility profiles.
context: Current rollout controller assumes a single, uniform canary step for all environments. Dedicated and Private environments have constraints (maintenance windows, tenant-affinity routing, network hairpins, limited egress, and KMS approval processes) that make identical canary behavior undesirable. Product needs: A/B experiments and shadow traffic in Hosted; restricted burst windows in Dedicated; and night-only rolling in Private. We need config parity at the API level while producing different runtime policies for each environment.
decisions: Use a canonical 'RolloutIntent' CRD in the control plane that is environment-agnostic. The adapter compiles a 'TrafficProfile' per environment at evaluation time.
Introduce time-window and tenant-affinity fields in rollout spec: exposure_windows (UTC ranges) and tenant_segments (regex or tenant lists).
Auto-rollback will operate on environment-specific SLOs and inverted success fences (hosted: 95th latency; dedicated: error-rate + saturation; private: security audit triggers).
Fallback behavior: if an environment lacks capacity for requested burst, the adapter reduces exposure and annotates the rollout with the reason.
progress_updates: 2025-03-02: Spike completed comparing latency distributions across environments; Dedicated shows higher variance under bursty traffic.
2025-03-05: Drafted RolloutIntent schema and posted design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Tenant-Windowed-Canary
2025-03-07: POC adapter that emits TrafficProfile JSON for Hosted/Dedicated/Private (internal branch: github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-adapter/tree/feature/tenant-windowed).
2025-03-10: Integration test harness can simulate 1K unique tenants with tenant-affinity routing; found race in KV-cache warmup which we marked as blocker for Dedicated.
acceptance_criteria: RolloutIntent API accepted and validated by Console UI (PM sign-off).
Adapter compiles TrafficProfile for each environment with capacity and window constraints encoded.
Auto-rollback triggers evaluated against env-specific SLOs and successfully reverts a canary in simulated failure scenarios.
End-to-end tests: Hosted A/B traffic split, Dedicated burst-limited window, Private night-only window pass in CI with synthetic tenants.
Documentation: Operator playbook and list of config knobs published to internal docs.
implementation_plan: Schema: Add RolloutIntent fields (exposure_windows, tenant_segments, env_overrides) — API change with backward compatibility.
Adapter: Build environment compiler that outputs TrafficProfile (percent, window, routing hints, resource_hints).
Controller: Extend rollout controller to evaluate TrafficProfile and call the traffic-shaper service with per-tenant rules.
Runtime: Update traffic-shaper to support tenant-affinity TTL and queued prefetched KV cache hints for burst windows.
Rollback: Wire env-specific metrics into the rollback evaluator and add annotated rollback reasons for operators.
Console: Add scheduling UI for exposure windows and tenant selection (small PM/UX changes).
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (Canary): Enable on internal 'lab' org in Hosted for A/B experiments with 1% exposure and 1-hour window.
Stage 2 (Scale tests): Run stress tests with Dedicated test pool with 10% tenant exposure but limited to 5-minute burst windows; monitor KV warmup.
Stage 3 (Private pilot): Deploy to a single Private customer with night-only windows and operator approval gate; run 2 rolling deployments.
Stage 4 (Gradual ramp): If no rollbacks, gradually increase exposure per tenant segment and triage any env-specific failures.
Abort conditions: auto-rollback on SLO breach or >0.5% critical errors in 5 minutes; manual abort threshold for Private placed with Solutions Eng.
test_plan: Unit tests for RolloutIntent validation and adapter compiler logic.
Integration tests in CI that spin up a local traffic-shaper mock and assert correct per-env TrafficProfile translations.
Chaos tests: Simulate backend saturation and network egress failures in Dedicated to validate graceful degradation and rollback.
E2E: Synthetic tenant cohort tests for Hosted A/B, Dedicated burst-limited, and Private night-only windows.
Performance: KV-cache warmup benchmark to ensure <50ms median additional latency for prefetched tenants.
Security: Verify Private operator approval flow (KMS sign-off) is required before exposure increases.
dependencies: ENG-13321 (kv-cache prefetch API and TTL extension)
PM-559 (Console scheduler UX for exposure windows)
risks: Dedicated capacity variance could cause false positive rollbacks if SLOs not tuned per env.
Complex tenant segmentation rules may cause inadvertent over-exposure if regex mis-specified.
KV-cache prefetch adds memory pressure in Dedicated pools leading to OOM if not capped.
Operator workflow for Private may slow rollouts significantly if approvals are required synchronously.
qa_checks: Run smoke canary for 24 hours on internal org and validate alert thresholds are firing correctly.
Verify audit logs capture RolloutIntent compilation decisions and reasons for any exposure reduction.
Confirm rollback annotated reasons appear in Console timeline and in incident exports.
